# html awaits t.wait where a test body writes it as a statement of its own,
# polling between turns of the page's event loop -- under one of the test's own
# `if`s too, which is lowered with the test statements in it, the way a trigger
# under a null test is.

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '--- PASS: /WaitsAtTheTop'
stdout '--- PASS: /WaitsInsideAnIf'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import "sngl:time"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component ticker ui.node {
    var n = 0
    time.timer(interval=10ms, enabled=true, @tick { n += 1 })
    ui.text(value="{n}")
}

func testWaitsAtTheTop(t Test, c ticker) {
    t.wait(func() => c.n >= 3, 2000)
    t.assert(c.n >= 3)
}

func testWaitsInsideAnIf(t Test, c ticker) {
    if c.n >= 0 {
        t.wait(func() => c.n >= 3, 2000)
    }
    t.assert(c.n >= 3)
}

ui.window {
    ticker
}
-- testrun/html/none/app.sngl/ticker/1 --

  "results": [
    {
      "Desc": "WaitsAtTheTop",
      "Passed": true
    },
    {
      "Desc": "WaitsInsideAnIf",
      "Passed": true
    }
  ]
}
